input.new_string:
<script>
  var toggle = document.getElementById('sort-toggle')
  var list = document.getElementById('sort-list')
  var label = document.getElementById('sort-label')
  var options = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.dd-option'))

  function setOpen(open) {
    list.classList.toggle('open', open)
    toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', open ? 'true' : 'false')
  }

  function closeList(returnFocus) {
    setOpen(false)
    if (returnFocus) toggle.focus()
  }

  function moveFocus(option) {
    options.forEach(function (o) { o.tabIndex = o === option ? 0 : -1 })
    option.focus()
  }

  function selectedOption() {
    return options.filter(function (o) { return o.getAttribute('aria-selected') === 'true' })[0] || options[0]
  }

  function commit(option) {
    options.forEach(function (o) { o.setAttribute('aria-selected', o === option ? 'true' : 'false') })
    label.textContent = 'Sort: ' + option.getAttribute('data-value')
  }

  toggle.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var open = !list.classList.contains('open')
    setOpen(open)
    if (open) moveFocus(selectedOption())
  })

  toggle.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    if ((e.key === 'ArrowDown' || e.key === 'Down') && !list.classList.contains('open')) {
      e.preventDefault()
      toggle.click()
    }
  })

  options.forEach(function (option, index) {
    option.addEventListener('click', function () {
      commit(option)
      closeList(true)
    })
    option.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
      switch (e.key) {
        case 'ArrowDown':
        case 'Down':
          e.preventDefault()
          moveFocus(options[Math.min(index + 1, options.length - 1)])
          break
        case 'ArrowUp':
        case 'Up':
          e.preventDefault()
          moveFocus(options[Math.max(index - 1, 0)])
          break
        case 'Home':
          e.preventDefault()
          moveFocus(options[0])
          break
        case 'End':
          e.preventDefault()
          moveFocus(options[options.length - 1])
          break
        case 'Enter':
        case ' ':
          e.preventDefault()
          option.click()
          break
        case 'Escape':
          e.preventDefault()
          closeList(true)
          break
        case 'Tab':
          setOpen(false)
          break
      }
    })
  })

  document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    if (list.classList.contains('open') && e.target !== toggle && !list.contains(e.target)) {
      setOpen(false)
    }
  })
</script>

content.text:
## Summary

The page had one interactive widget — a "Sort" dropdown — built entirely from `<div>`s with only a mouse `click` handler. That's the source of every defect:

**Defects found**
- `.dd-toggle` and `.dd-option` were plain `div`s: not focusable, no keyboard support, no accessible role/name/state, no visible focus indicator (they couldn't even receive focus).
- No `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` on the toggle, no `role="listbox"`/`role="option"`/`aria-selected` on the list, so assistive tech had no idea a menu existed or what was selected.
- No Escape-to-close, no arrow-key navigation, no return-of-focus to the toggle after a selection.
- The decorative caret glyph ("v") would have been read aloud by screen readers.

**Fixes made**
- Changed `.dd-toggle` from a `div` to a real `<button type="button">`, keeping its `id`, `data-track`, and CSS class so styling and instrumentation are untouched. This gives native Tab reachability and Enter/Space activation for free.
- Added `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls="sort-list"` to the toggle; `role="listbox"` + `aria-label="Sort by"` on the list; `role="option"` + `aria-selected` on each option (options stayed `div`s, per the "keep custom widgets custom" constraint).
- Implemented the ARIA listbox pattern with a roving `tabindex`: opening the list moves focus to the current selection; ArrowUp/Down/Home/End move focus among options; Enter/Space calls the option's own `.click()` (so keyboard and mouse share one code path and instrumentation fires identically); Escape and Tab close the list and Escape/commit return focus to the toggle button.
- Hid the decorative caret from assistive tech with `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Added explicit visible `:focus`/`:focus-visible` outlines for the toggle, options, and result links.
- Reset `font`/`color` inheritance on the new `<button>` so it renders identically to the old `div`.

**Left alone**
- All visible text, layout, color palette (contrast on existing text/link colors was already ≥ 4.5:1, verified by calculation), the instrumentation script, and all `id`/`data-track` attributes, which remain on the same conceptual elements.
- Result links were already plain `<a href>`s with correct semantics, so no changes were needed there beyond the shared focus-style rule.

No browser/axe runner was available in this sandbox, so verification was done by manual trace of the DOM/ARIA tree, contrast math, and a full keyboard walkthrough (Tab order, Enter/Space, arrow keys, Escape, focus return) against the contract's requirements.
